title: Brother's rehearsals and his first paid job
summary: His brother's band rehearsed at home; Purnell got his first job as a singer and two-piece pianist during the depression and was paid fifteen dollars.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Was your brother already playing something that?

Yeah. My brother at that time had begun to take up the saxophone and we were living together. And oh they used to have ten and fifteen fellas every day used to rehearse them back there. They rehearsed them so much that I knew a number from the introduction to the corner stop. I could whistle it, I mean without making a mistake. But anyhow he became a very wonderful musician and I'm very proud of him. He was one of the top saxophone players down in New Orleans, which I think he still is if he can still play. But me I wanted to battle house, you know, and he wanted me to take music. In fact one time he tried to learn me how to play the saxophone. And man I'm telling you we laughed so much I never could get nothing. He would kid me and I would laugh and he would laugh and I just quit. But the first job I ever got was with, I was standing on the corner and things was tough during the depression. And some people came down looking for a piano player. Well I couldn't play over two pieces but I could sing a lot you know. And they were looking for this piano player George E. Parker. And they asked me did I know where he was. So I told them well I knew a couple of places that he might be. So I got in the car with them and went looking for him and we never could find him. So one of the fellas mentioned said we just could find a fella who could play one or two pieces. So I told them I could play one or two pieces. So they said well that's good enough. And we went well around the lake which I was lost when I got out there. And I really did a good job. The singing really put me over you know. That was your first job.
My first job. You got paid for it.

Yeah wait the trouble was when I knocked off the man asked me how much did he owe me. And I didn't know what to charge him. And I needed money so badly. But I said ten dollars you know. And which was very high at that time. You just wasn't getting that kind of money. But I didn't know what to charge so I said ten dollars. You know I wanted to be a big shot. So the man gave me fifteen dollars anyhow. And I was rich man. Yeah that was good.
